builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
summary: The method replaces BF16 or generic one-size-fits-all 4-bit post-training quantization with format-dependent recipes combining microscaling formats (MXFP4, MXFP6, NVFP4), Hadamard rotation, error-correcting PTQ, and the calibration-free Midmax scale selection for power-of-two block scales. Costs are added PTQ pipeline complexity, per-format tuning effort, and modest activation memory overhead if MXFP6 activations are used to recover accuracy; Midmax itself adds no calibration cost. Failure modes include applying MXFP4-tuned techniques (rotation, error-correcting PTQ) to NVFP4 where they yield little benefit, relying on per-tensor macroscales that the paper shows do not help MXFP4, and residual clipping error from E8M0 block scales on outlier-heavy models.
rationale: Format-specific 4-bit PTQ recipes with a calibration-free scale-selection option let a single 24 GB GPU run larger models at BF16-comparable quality without retraining.
technique: Format-dependent MXFP4/NVFP4 PTQ with Midmax scaling

claims.statement: The method replaces BF16 or generic one-size-fits-all 4-bit post-training quantization with format-dependent recipes combining microscaling formats (MXFP4, MXFP6, NVFP4), Hadamard rotation, error-correcting PTQ, and the calibration-free Midmax scale selection for power-of-two block scales. Costs are added PTQ pipeline complexity, per-format tuning effort, and modest activation memory overhead if MXFP6 activations are used to recover accuracy; Midmax itself adds no calibration cost. Failure modes include applying MXFP4-tuned techniques (rotation, error-correcting PTQ) to NVFP4 where they yield little benefit, relying on per-tensor macroscales that the paper shows do not help MXFP4, and residual clipping error from E8M0 block scales on outlier-heavy models.

Pairing MXFP6 activations with MXFP4 weights recovers most of the accuracy lost at 4-bit and, on Llama-3.1-8B, matches or exceeds the authors' in-house BF16 baseline; the Midmax scale-selection strategy improves accuracy across a majority of evaluated MXFP4 configurations.
